sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mobile Utility Software and Device Performance Optimization Apps

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English Common Law foundation with Samoan customary law elements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Samoa–New Zealand Double Taxation Agreement (2012, in force)
PACER-Plus Agreement on Regional Trade and Economic Partnership (in force since 2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended); International Companies Act 1987 (as amended); Financial Institutions Act 1996 (as amended); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism directives issued by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) and the Central Bank of Samoa; Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) mutual evaluation obligations

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid passport for each director, shareholder, and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority in country of origin, with notarization by a licensed notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) for each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming banking history for each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing licensed bank in country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate due diligence pack for any corporate shareholder (certificate of incorporation, register of directors, UBO register extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry and registered agent in the jurisdiction of incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated List, US OFAC SDN and consolidated non-SDN lists, UK HMT sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, and Samoa's domestic sanctions and proscribed persons lists, using an international screening database such as Dow Jones or Refinitiv World-Check. Any PEP or sanctions match triggers enhanced due diligence (EDD), senior management approval, and source-of-funds verification. Re-screening is required at least annually and upon any trigger event.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — International Companies Registry (name search and reservation filed through licensed registered agents via the SIFA portal, sifa.ws)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered company name must be expressed in Latin (Roman) script. Non-Roman names, including Chinese-language commercial names, must be accompanied by a certified transliteration into English or Roman characters for the registry record. Constitutional documents may be drafted in Chinese, but the certificate of incorporation and registry records will reflect the Romanized name. Samoan-language names follow standard Samoan orthography.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the licensed registered agent must file a written review submission with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days, stating the statutory grounds for reversal. If the rejection is based on a prohibited or sensitive token, an application for ministerial dispensation may be lodged with the Minister of Commerce where the International Companies Act 1987 permits. A further appeal lies by way of judicial review to the Supreme Court of Samoa. A reserved name may be extended by filing a fresh reservation application before the initial 30-day window expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office operations are permissible for the business activity of mobile utility app development and distribution, but the statutory registered office must be maintained at a physical address in Samoa through a licensed registered agent. A pure virtual or co-working address does not satisfy the International Companies Act 1987 requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated less than 5% annual probability absent trigger events such as regulatory complaints, FIU queries, or sanctions hits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Customer due diligence and UBO vetting fee
Notarization of UBO and director document bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in country of document origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization chain for certified documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and consular posts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark and consular tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 2016 of Samoa; ss. 6-9 (Incorporation Procedures), s. 12 (Registered Office), ss. 13-15 (Registered Agent), s. 18 (Name Restrictions), s. 24 (Memorandum and Articles), s. 25 (Certificate of Incorporation), ss. 130-132 (Fees and Penalties)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued upon filing of the Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form IC-02 (Application for Incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an International Company; standard authorized capital of US$100,000 (or such larger amount as desired) divided into shares of no par value, with at least one share issued and fully paid; no escrow account or capital deposit redemption requirement is imposed on non-resident founders
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The following resolutions are adopted by the subscriber and the initial director of the International Company: 1. Constitution: The Memorandum and Articles of Association filed with the Registrar are adopted. 2. Share Subscription: The subscriber subscribes for one ordinary share of the US$100,000 authorized capital, and the initial director allots the share fully paid at par. 3. Registered Office: The registered office and postal address provided by the licensed registered agent are adopted. 4. Officers: [Name] is appointed Director and [Name] Corporate Secretary, each serving until removed. 5. Banking and General: The Director may open bank accounts, sign digital service agreements, and instruct the registered agent to effect filings necessary to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — Name Reservation Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an Application for Reservation of Name (Form IC-01) listing up to three proposed corporate names in priority order, together with the notarized identification of the proposed director/shareholder and the written consent of the licensed registered agent. The Registrar searches the national company names register and rejects prohibited names under s. 18 of the International Companies Act 2016. A successful reservation is held for 60 days pending submission of the incorporation documents.
required_dossiers: Application for Reservation of Name (Form IC-01)
Notarized copy of passport of each proposed director and shareholder
Statement of proposed business scope referencing ISIC 6201
Licensed registered agent consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the applicant may file an alternative name list or submit a written appeal to the Registrar within 14 days; prohibited words may be removed without additional fee and the application resubmitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent in Samoa (SIFA-licensed corporate services provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association reflecting the reserved name, authorized capital of US$100,000 (or chosen amount), share classes, director and secretary details, and the proposed registered office. The sole subscriber executes the document in the presence of a Notary Public; the Declaration of Compliance and consents to act are signed and certified contemporaneously.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (signed)
Declaration of Compliance under s. 8 of the International Companies Act 2016
Consent to act as Director (Form IC-03)
Consent to act as Secretary (Form IC-04)
Notarized subscriber signature page
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any notarial or signature defects by re-execution; if the registered agent's compliance policy requires an apostille or attestation, such authentication shall be obtained from the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade before submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent submits the complete incorporation package via the SIFA e-registration portal or by in-person lodgment at the SIFA counter. The submission comprises Form IC-02 (Application for Incorporation), the executed Memorandum and Articles, all notarized declarations and consents, the registered office and agent appointment letter, and the fee computation sheet based on authorized capital.
required_dossiers: Form IC-02 (Application for Incorporation)
Memorandum and Articles of Association (signed and notarized)
Declaration of Compliance and officer consents
Registered office and registered agent appointment letter
Fee computation sheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the registered agent files a supplemental declaration or corrective amendment within 10 working days; SIFA may impose a nominal US$50 resubmission fee; if the conflict involves the agent, a new licensed registered agent is appointed and the appointment filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority — Finance and Corporate Affairs Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the incorporation registration fee of US$500 (for authorized capital not exceeding US$100,000), the first-year annual government fee of US$300, and the carrying trade fee of US$100 (IT/software service classification). All fees are remitted by international bank wire transfer to SIFA's Trust Account or by certified cheque; the remittance advice and SWIFT confirmation are retained in the company's statutory records.
required_dossiers: SIFA pro-forma invoice on fee assessment
International bank transfer remittance advice / SWIFT receipt
Certified cheque counterfoil (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Reconcile discrepancies by presenting the SWIFT advice to SIFA Finance; late payment interest accrues under s. 132 of the Act; a formal receipt must be obtained before collecting the Certificate of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review and fee clearance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation dated as of the day of registration. The registered agent collects the certificate on behalf of the company; the certificate is authenticated under SIFA's common seal and constitutes conclusive evidence of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Approved incorporation application file
Proof of full fee payment
Registered agent collection authorization letter
Identity verification of the agent's courier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains clerical errors, apply for rectification under s. 67 of the Act; SIFA issues a corrected certificate within 3 working days without additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial Director acting by written resolution; SIFA-licensed registered agent; licensed commercial bank in Samoa or licensed foreign bank accepting International Company accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the First Board Resolution adopting the constitution, approving the share allotment, adopting the registered office, and appointing officers. File the Appointment of Director/Secretary forms (Form IC-05) with the Registrar within 14 days of appointment. Open the corporate bank account with the Certificate of Incorporation, the board resolution, and the AML/KYC package for the beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution (as set out above)
Form IC-05 (Appointment of Directors and Secretary)
Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
Registered agent confirmation of office address
AML/KYC package for bank account opening (passport, proof of address, source of funds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For late filing of officer particulars, submit a late-filing declaration and pay the US$100 penalty; if the bank rejects KYC submissions, provide updated beneficial ownership registers and re-submit through a licensed bank relationship manager.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) — Business and Industrial Licensing Division (relevant only if the company were to engage in domestic physical trading; International Companies operating under ISIC 6201 are statutorily exempt from domestic industrial licensing)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — an International Company conducting pure mobile utility software development, distribution, and maintenance under ISIC 6201 holds no manufacturing plant or physical industrial installation, and therefore no operating license or manufacturing permit is issued or demanded under Samoan industrial legislation

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa — Environment and Conservation Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Low-Impact Digital Service — no physical earthworks, industrial plant, effluent outfall, or atmospheric emission sources are associated with software coding, App Store distribution, or cloud-based device performance optimization; should the company later deploy colocation server infrastructure, a Preliminary EIA (Category B) may be triggered under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2016
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or particulate discharge thresholds apply to pure software operations; any electronic waste from replaced IT hardware must be handled in accordance with the Waste Management Act 2017 and relevant MNRE waste disposal guidelines; if a data center or server room is operated in Samoa, thermal discharge and electrical safety must comply with AS/NZS 61439 and MNRE best-practice covenants

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for the standard registered-agent virtual office model. If a physical office is maintained in Samoa: (1) a Fire Safety Certificate must be obtained from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority; (2) structural load and building clearance from the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure; (3) workplace occupational clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2011 covering workstations, electrical installations, and fire egress routes.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue, Government of Samoa (formerly Inland Revenue Department); online portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must complete the Samoa Tax Identification Number (TIN) application through the Ministry of Revenue's online registration facility, submitting a certified copy of the incorporation certificate, passport of directors, and proof of registered office. Inbound entities that will engage in taxable supplies must also complete a VAT/VAGST registration application on the same portal, providing the TIN, business details, and turnover projections. International Companies are exempt from income tax and are not ordinarily registered for income tax; they may, however, apply for a non-resident or exempt status certificate from the Ministry of Revenue where required by counterparties or banks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or partnership classification elections exist under Samoa tax law. The International Company's tax-exempt status is mandatory and automatic under the International Companies Act 1987, not elective. No hybrid mismatch or branch-equivalent elections are provided by Samoa's domestic legislation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration for any business making taxable supplies exceeding WST 100,000 in any 12-month period; voluntary registration is available below threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate in Samoa. Registered suppliers must issue an invoice (in paper or electronic form) containing prescribed content under the Goods and Services Tax Act 2003 and retain it for audit; no government clearance platform is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered supplier may zero-rate a supply where it is a direct export of tangible goods (i.e., goods delivered outside Samoa and exported within 28 days of supply) or an international service supplied to a non-resident who consumes the services wholly outside Samoa, or where the supply is made in connection with goods for export. The supplier must hold documentary evidence proving export, receipt by the foreign customer, and actual receipt of payment from a source outside Samoa. Zero-rating is denied where the goods or services are consumed in Samoa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Customs Entry / Export Entry Number)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (signed by carrier)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing foreign exchange receipt from the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry of Revenue may scrutinize zero-rated export claims retrospectively. An erroneous or fraudulent zero-rating claim triggers full clawback of the refund, plus interest at the late-payment rate, and a civil shortfall penalty of up to 200% of the undeclared tax. Wilful evasion carries criminal prosecution with fines up to WST 200,000 and imprisonment up to 12 months for individuals, and directors may be personally liable for penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Exchange Control Authority under the Exchange Control Act 1975 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1985; supervises all authorized dealers in foreign exchange, approves all capital account transactions, and administers Samoa's national payments and settlement infrastructure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa's national currency, the WST (Tala), is partially convertible. Current account transactions (e.g., software licensing royalties, developer payments, app store disbursements, ongoing operational expenses) are generally permitted for authorized dealers. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity injections, shareholder loans, loan repayments, and repatriation of invested capital, require Exchange Control approval from the Central Bank of Samoa. Non-resident holders of an International Company (IC) may freely remit current-account profits and dividends after submission of audited financial statements and payment of applicable Samoa income tax; however, capital repatriation is subject to a documented trail of approved capital importation and CBS prior approval to ensure historical currency purchase validation. While the WST is not freely deliverable offshore, commercial banks quote onshore rates within CBS statutory margins; all FX transactions must be executed through an authorized dealer unless an explicit exemption has been granted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds derived from goods and services, including mobile app gross revenue remitted to Samoa, must be collected within 6 months of shipment or the date the obligation arises, and must be offered for sale to an authorized dealer in Samoa within 30 days of receipt in foreign currency. The mandatory conversion ratio is 100%, meaning all foreign currency received from export sales must be converted to WST at the applicable bank selling rate, unless the IC has secured a CBS foreign currency retention allowance (typically 25%–50% of eligible foreign currency inflows) for operational liquidity or an approved ring-fenced foreign currency account for trade settlement. Receipts supporting the Samoa IC's digital application business must be evidenced by the App Store OR Google Play settlement statements and reported to the Central Bank through the commercial bank on a monthly basis. Unconverted retention balances require quarterly justification requests.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (Samoa) Limited (ANZ Samoa)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Foreign Currency + WST Account / Capital Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) Limited (BSP Samoa)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD/EUR Account and WST domestic clearing account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility of using offshore digital financial institutions (EMI) or digital banks as treasury side-rails is rated LOW for the core Samoa IC. The Central Bank of Samoa restricts maintained licenses to authorized banking institutions; no recognized licensing pathway exists for an EMI domiciled in the EEA or Hong Kong to act as the IC's primary settlement bank. Offshore EMIs may be used only as complementary billing corridors for utility-application in-app purchases through Stripe/Adyen acquiring partners that route via Apple Pay and Google Pay; they cannot legally be used to hold WST balances, must not conduct FX conversion on behalf of a Samoa IC, and cannot clear any Samoa Export Proceeds surrender obligations. Physical correspondent banking relationships at ANZ or BSP will remain the sole regulated conduit for both WST and USD current account activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an International Company with nominee shareholders and a purely digital mobile-app business, Samoa banks require full KYC/CDD interviews. In practice, at least one executive director, and, if advisable, the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), must appear in person at the bank's Apia branch for initial account sign-off; a video conference or notarized interview is only accepted when the natural person resides in a jurisdiction without a Samoan embassy or recognized reputable banking channel. The bank will require the original certificate of incorporation, the IC's memorandum and articles, the Certificate of Good Standing, a registered office certificate, and an IRS Form 6166/TRC or Samoa tax clearance certificate where applicable. Fully remote account opening is not available for the IC's first account; subsequent signatory updates can be handled by an authorized representative using CBS-compliant forms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: opening a low-revenue, pre-profits mobile app company with immediate physically mandatory bank interview and no prior Samoan tax history, which can trigger a false positive risk of shell entity classification under FATF recommendations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a two-year mobile app profit-and-loss projection, presentation of the App Store/Google Play monetization model, commercial agreements with app stores, a source-of-funds declaration, definitive shareholder/UBO register, organizational chart showing the IC's place within the WS_IC family structure, CES certified independent legal counsel opinion, registered office contract, and a written mitigation statement of no local physical footprint in Samoa.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: identification of UBO with a tax residency in a blacklisted or grey-listed jurisdiction, or a nominee equity structure inconsistent with economic substance disclosures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full beneficiary ownership register (BOR), trust deed and trust letter of wishes, a residency declaration for each ultimate owner, certified passport copies, proof of residential address, current bank and employer references, and a completed Samoa Inland Revenue standard declaration of tax residency. Include a one-to-one explanation of each nominee's legal role and evidence that no non-compliant bearer shares exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: inbound remittances from mobile app store aggregators routed through high-risk or crypto-adjacent PSPs require enhanced due diligence and could result in a hard block if unidentified third-party commercial relationships appear.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit executed settlement agreements with Apple and Google (or recognized application monetization platforms), a formal no-virtual-assets policy, a copy of the entity-level AML policy and procedure manual, a detailed reconciliation of historical store settlement reports, purpose codes for any incoming technical payments, and a complete commercial invoice register demonstrating arm's length fees paid for software development, cloud infrastructure, and royalties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections to the Samoa International Company must be routed as SWIFT MT103 transfers from the parent treasury account to the designated ANZ Samoa or BSP Samoa foreign currency account, with the full legal entity name WS_IC as beneficiary. Prior to the first wire, the IC must file a Capital Importation Application with the Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) through its account officer and obtain an Exchange Control approval certificate, which must be quoted in SWIFT field 70 (Remittance Information). To support conversion, the incoming wire should indicate a documented purpose code consistent with the Samoa Exchange Control Manual, such as 'C.1. Inward Investment – Equity Capital' or 'C.2. Intercompany Loan Facility'. For amounts exceeding USD 50,000, the bank will require a board resolution, a source-of-wealth declaration from final UBO, evidence that the sender is compliant with the ISIC 6201 app software development scope, and a copy of the approved CBS inbound application. Any loan-related injection must be accompanied by a signed and stamped intercompany loan agreement, a repayment schedule, and agreement to use an arm's length interest rate consistent with the 2023 OECD TP guidelines.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for the mobile utility app's trade-related disbursements – cloud hosting, SaaS licences, SDK licensing, online advertising, app optimization contractors, and professional development fees – must be executed via SWIFT MT103 direct transfers from the IC's USD or WST bank account. A commercial letter of credit (LC) is appropriate only for high-value hardware purchases (e.g., server racks, colocations, specialized telecommunication equipment) with a trade finance facility through ANZ or BSP; in that case the LC must contain a conventional 90 days-usance clause, an inspection certificate, and bills of lading that align with the ISIC 6201 activity code. For each MT103 disbursement, the applicant must submit a relevant commercial invoice, a statement of service or contractor certificate, a CBS Outward Foreign Exchange Application (Form CE-2), and an exchange control approval, if the transfer exceeds WST 100,000 equivalent. All outbound trade settlements must state the correct ISO 20022 purpose code, e.g.,
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.for royalties or: for contracted services, and the correspondent chain must utilise the Samoa Interbank Settlement System (SISS) for WST legs and SWIFT via the bank's Sydney, New York or London correspondents for USD, GBP and EUR legs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards on USD/WST for approved current account exposures, maximum tenor 365 days, no net open speculative position.
Discounted Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on USD/WST executed only through a licensed authorized dealer in Samoa for hedging of non-convertible country risk exposures.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/WST and USD/EUR) for trade settlements and intercompany capital flows, subject to CBS economic purpose validation.
FX options (European style) for treasury hedging of app-store revenue repatriation risks, permitted only after a documented hedge rationale and monthly reporting to the Central Bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Annual Licence Fee (Form IC-AR) of the International Company, including current registered office, registered agent, directors, shareholders, share capital, and the registered agent's certificate of statutory-register compliance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary date of incorporation each year; if SIFA exercises discretion, no later than 30 days after the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment penalty of 10% of the overdue amount for each month or part-month of delay. If the Annual Return and licence fee remain unpaid for 6 months after the due date, the Registrar may strike the company off the International Companies Register without judicial proceedings. Restoration requires payment of all arrears, penalties, and a formal restoration application.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (UBO schedule) included with the Annual Return and certified by the registered agent.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFA; accessible to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit under AML/CFT information-exchange rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not a separate filing; must accompany the Annual Return and be current as at the incorporation anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit an accurate UBO schedule renders the Annual Return incomplete and triggers the same late-filing penalty and strike-off risk as the Annual Return. Knowingly false UBO information is an offence punishable by fine and/or imprisonment under Samoa AML/CFT legislation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit applies to a standard non-resident International Company engaged in unlicensed software activity; no turnover, asset, or shareholder threshold automatically triggers an audit. Mandatory independent audit is required only for International Companies licensed or supervised by SIFA as banks, insurers, trust providers, fund administrators, securities dealers, or money service businesses, or where SIFA imposes an audit condition on a specific licence or order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) are mandatory for SIFA-licensed entities. Ordinary International Companies are not required to apply a prescribed framework, but accounting records must be kept with sufficient accuracy to explain transactions and present a reasonable picture of financial position; such records are not filed with the Registrar.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must maintain the Register of Beneficial Owners at the Samoa registered office and include a current UBO schedule in each Annual Return. Any share transfer must be approved by the directors, recorded in the Register of Members, and reflected in the Register of Beneficial Owners before the transferee's title is recognised; contemporaneous updating is required, and an annual wait is not permitted. For each transfer, the registered agent must verify the transferee's identity and ultimate beneficial owner, update the register within 14 days, and make the transfer data available to SIFA upon inspection.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 750 - USD 1,500 per year for a standard International Company, including Samoa registered office, licensed registered agent, and Annual Return handling.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 6,000 per audit engagement for a small non-public International Company when an audit is required by a lender, investor, or SIFA condition.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% standard corporate income tax rate applied to resident companies under the Samoa Income Tax Act 2012; International Companies (ICs) registered under the International Companies Act 1987-88 are statutorily exempt from Samoan income tax on all international business income, resulting in an effective rate of 0% for the subject mobile App Store revenue.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption from corporate income tax, capital gains tax, dividend withholding tax, and stamp duty on share transfers for International Companies (International Companies Act 1987-88, s. 201 (exemption provision), as amended). No tax holiday application is required; the exemption is automatic upon valid IC registration and payment of the annual government fee. Onshore companies may access a 10-year investment incentive holiday under the Incentives Act 2012, but this is irrelevant to a tax-exempt IC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Form ICA-7) filed electronically through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) e-portal; no corporate income tax return is filed for an exempt IC because no assessable Samoan income exists. Filings are submitted by the SIFA-licensed registered agent on the company's behalf.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 90 days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation; the same due date governs the payment of the annual government fee (licence renewal). No quarterly instalments apply to exempt ICs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name of the International Company as it appears on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the registered English name; a name change requires prior approval of the Registrar plus payment of the name-change fee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique IC registration number assigned by SIFA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the number exactly; errors delay SIFA's processing and trigger a rejection notice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Street address of the registered office in Apia maintained by the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A physical Samoan street address is mandatory; a P.O. Box is insufficient. Non-resident entities cannot maintain the registered office directly; the licensed agent's address must be stated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and licence number of the SIFA-licensed registered agent or trust company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent must be a licensed Samoan trust company; the agent signs the Annual Return and is jointly liable for statutory obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, nationalities, residential addresses, and passport numbers of all directors and the corporate secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are permitted; provide certified passport copies and a CV for beneficial ownership files. Nationality of each director must be stated for AML screening.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of shareholders, class and number of shares, and location of the share register and beneficial ownership register.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Corporate and nominee shareholders are permitted. Issued capital may be as low as USD 1 (no minimum capital). Beneficial owner particulars must be disclosed to the agent; bearer shares are restricted and must be immobilized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Declaration of No Samoan-Source Business
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory declaration confirming the IC has not engaged in domestic trade with Samoa residents, has not beneficially owned Samoan land, and carries on business only outside Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This declaration is the foundation of the tax exemption. A false declaration exposes the IC to the 27% corporate tax, a 100% evasion penalty, and personal liability of the signing director.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the annual government fee (computed from authorised share capital under the International Companies (Government Fees) Regulations) has been paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payable in WST via SIFA portal by the due date. Payment is evidenced by a receipt reference inserted into the Return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is penalized by a surcharge equal to 10% of the annual government fee per commenced month (or partial month), capped at 100% of the fee; no daily per diem applies. Persistent non-filing for 6 months triggers a peremptory notice from the Registrar and strike-off of the IC. Late payment of the annual government fee carries the same 10% monthly penalty, and restoration after strike-off requires payment of all outstanding fees, penalties, and a restoration fee.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends resolved and paid by an International Company, because IC-distributed dividends are outside the scope of Samoa's 15% withholding tax imposed on resident companies under the Income Tax Act 2012 (s. 111). The general statutory rate of 15% applies only to dividends paid by non-exempt resident companies to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For an exempt IC, no treaty protocol is required and the 0% domestic exemption applies automatically. For any shareholder or related entity relying on a Samoa income tax treaty (e.g., treaties with Australia, New Zealand, China) to reduce the 15% statutory withholding rates, the paying entity must file the prescribed withholding tax return with the Ministry of Revenue, attaching: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, (ii) a certificate of beneficial ownership, and (iii) a completed treaty entitlement declaration, all submitted within 30 days of the payment. If the documents are not furnished on time, the full 15% rate applies and a refund claim may be lodged within 3 years of the date of payment pursuant to the Tax Administration Act 2012.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty and interest withholding tax to non-residents is 15% under the Income Tax Act 2012. Treaty rates generally reduce interest and royalties to 10% where the recipient is the beneficial owner (subject to domestic anti-treaty-shopping rules). For International Companies, interest earned and royalties received from international business are statutorily exempt at 0%, and Samoa imposes no withholding on payments of interest or royalties made by an IC to non-residents.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa does not prescribe formal Local File/Master File thresholds expressed in Samoan Tala (WST), and exempt International Companies have no mandatory TP documentation obligations unless they lose exempt status. The Income Tax Act 2012 incorporates the arm's length principle for cross-border related-party transactions of taxable entities, and the Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue may require contemporaneous TP documentation on audit where aggregate related-party turnover is material. The OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines are used as interpretative guidance. For the subject IC, the practical benchmark is to maintain internal pricing records for the App Store royalty split between the IP owner and the platform operator (Apple/Google) and for any management fee paid to an affiliate.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2019 and accompanying Regulations apply to Samoa International Companies conducting 'relevant activities'. If the mobile utility app business is structured such that the IC owns the software IP and licenses it to app stores, the activity may fall under the 'intellectual property holding' relevant activity, which requires a high-threshold economic substance test: demonstrable active management at Samoan board level, decisions on development, maintenance, and enhancement of the IP made in Samoa, adequate qualified local employees, physical premises, and expenditure proportionate to the IP income. If structured purely as a digital distribution business, the activity is less likely to be a listed relevant activity; however, the IC must in all cases avoid trading with Samoan residents and preserve documentary evidence of commercial reality. Maintenance of a Samoan registered agent alone does not constitute substance; the IC must have a physical Apia office, a local bank account, a Samoan-resident director or manager with decision-making authority, and board minutes executed in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting business with Samoan residents, invoicing Samoan customers for the mobile app, owning an interest in Samoan land, or otherwise deriving Samoan-source income outside the International Companies Act exemption. A false declaration in Box 7 of the Annual Return is treated as fraudulent evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Loss of the full income tax exemption with immediate reassessment of all assessable income at 27%; addition of a 100% evaded-tax penalty under the Tax Administration Act 2012; interest accrual at the statutory rate; publication of the IC in the 'Defaulting International Companies' gazette; criminal conviction carrying a fine of up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years for the company's officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for fraudulent trading: the Court may order directors jointly and severally liable for all unpaid tax, penalties, and creditor debts. Directors who signed a false declaration face personal fines, asset forfeiture orders, travel bans enforced at Samoa's ports of entry, and terms of imprisonment for each false statutory declaration made.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC receives App Store proceeds from software IP but has no Samoan presence beyond a registered agent, no local board meetings, no employees, no physical premises, and no records of core income-generating activities in Samoa, in breach of the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2019.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of up to WST 20,000 for the first contravention and WST 50,000 for repeated contravention, plus a daily default penalty; the SIFA may strike the IC off the register and will exchange information with the beneficial owner's tax residence authority under Samoa's international tax information exchange agreements. The IC's bank account may be blocked by SIFA order pending compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly consenting to the false substance declaration are deemed personally liable for the penalty, may be disqualified from acting as directors of any Samoan international company for up to 10 years, and are subject to travel bans and criminal fines up to WST 50,000. Restitution to the government for fees improperly retained or repatriated may be ordered against their personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register the natural-person beneficial owner with the licensed agent, concealment of app-store revenue derived from fraudulent schemes, use of the IC's bank account as a money-laundering conduit, or failure to file Suspicious Transaction Reports with Samoa's Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2018.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties up to WST 500,000 against the IC; confiscation of the account balance and connected assets under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2018; revocation of the registered agent's licence (resulting in automatic strike-off of the IC if no replacement agent is appointed within 30 days).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers knowingly involved in laundering proceeds face criminal liability: imprisonment of up to 10 years and fines of up to WST 1,000,000. Personal civil restitution is ordered for funds traced through the company; travel bans are automatic upon the FIU's issuance of a notification to the Immigration Division, and forfeiture of personal assets is available where the company is a facade for the director's benefit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Annual Return and Government Fee Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the International Company Annual Return or to pay the annual government fee by the 90-day anniversary deadline, causing the company to fall into arrears with SIFA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Accrual of the 10% monthly late-payment penalty (capped at 100% of the fee); issuance of a peremptory strike-off notice; deregistration after six months' continued default, at which point all contracts and assets of the IC vest in the Registrar for realisation. A struck-off IC cannot appear in app store agreements, and Apple/Google may terminate the developer account for loss of corporate existence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally and jointly liable for all unpaid annual fees, late penalties, and restoration costs incurred to reinstate the IC; the Registrar may issue a certificate of debt enforceable against the directors' personal property. Repeated default subjects directors to a travel ban, disqualification from managing any Samoa company for 5 years, and civil restitution for assets dissipated after the company became insolvent.
